name: Ontario statutes on e-Laws: 242 of the 1288 consolidated public statutes e-Laws lists (current and repealed), 0 of them repealed within the record

scope.when_absent: this corpus records no scope notes (no commit carries Applies:); the absence is not a statement that the change reaches every case

default_reach.rule: presumption against retrospectivity; immediate application to procedure
default_reach.meaning: an enactment is presumed not to apply to facts completed before it came into force, or to interfere with vested rights, unless the Legislature says so expressly or by necessary implication; a repeal does not affect the previous operation of the repealed Act, rights or liabilities that came into existence under it, or offences committed against it; proceedings continue under the new or amended Act, whose procedure applies to matters that happened before; where the new Act provides a lesser penalty, the lesser one applies
default_reach.authority: Legislation Act, 2006, S.O. 2006, c. 21, Sched. F, s. 51 (effect of repeal and revocation) and s. 52 (effect of amendment and replacement); Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s. 11(g) and 11(i); R. v. Dineley, 2012 SCC 58, [2012] 3 S.C.R. 272

label: Ontario
record_note: Checked against the official source on 2026-11-05: every point-in-time version on e-Laws of each act in the record, file by file and by letters and digits against the raw text. English text in force only (text of amendments not yet in force is left out). Each act starts with its first point-in-time version on e-Laws (2000s for most older acts), so earlier history is not in the record. The first four acts were built in date order (2026-10-29); every other act was appended later as its own block of commits (an end block: its dates run back from the commits above it; date each version by In-force, never by commit order). 0 acts repealed before their first version are not in it. Regulations are not included.
path_pattern: <e-Laws id>/s-<section, whole part padded to 3 digits>.md; <e-Laws id>/schedule[-<n>].md; <e-Laws id>/intro.md
